title: engineer-cadence-coaching-brief-priya-nair-mar09-2027
content:
Purpose
- Quick prep for 30m cadence with Eli Torres (IC-2). Keep it light, prioritize unblocked work and career temperature. Aim: leave with 2–3 concrete actions and a coaching moment.

Background/context
- Eli owns KV cache improvements on the serving runtime. Recently blocked by INF-3245 (async flush interaction) and needs cross-team test infra help.
- Last conversation (2 weeks ago): agreed to prototype fallback for cold-cache misses and pair with infra on a smoke test.
- Current velocity: 60–70% of expected; shipping slowed by test coverage and flakiness.

Agenda (30m)
- 0–5m: personal check-in (non-work) — quick mood & energy (what's taking headspace).
- 5–12m: project status (KV cache prototype + INF-3245) — What shipped, what's flaky, timeline estimate.
- 12–20m: unblock plan — who do we need help from (infra/qa)? Concrete next steps to unblock this week.
- 20–27m: career/feedback — 1 strength, 1 growth area; ask about stretch goals for next quarter.
- 27–30m: recap & actions.

Prep notes / cues (manager mindset)
- Be curious, not prescriptive. Let Eli voice inferred blockers before offering solutions.
- Use Socratic questions: "What did you try?" "What's the smallest experiment that tells us we're moving forward?" "Who do you want me to ping if infra doesn't respond?"
- Specific coaching: focus on stakeholder signals — ask Eli to frame one key metric customers will see improve after this change.

Project: KV cache async flush (INF-3245) — quick status
- Current: prototype branch merged to feature/kvcache-async (PR referenced). Observed flakiness in multi-az test matrix — flakiness spikes when sequence length > 1024.
- Recent test run: 62% pass across suite (should be >95%). Failing tests are deterministic in reproducer but nondeterministic in CI.
- Hypothesis: race in KV eviction path interacting with compiled kernels on newer CUDA drivers.

Immediate unblock ideas (ranked quick wins)
1) Narrow repro & deterministic harness (owner: Eli) — isolate a minimal reproducer and add it to local harness. Goal: by EOD Thu.
2) Infra pairing session (owner: Priya + infra lead Noah) — 2h deep-dive to run tests against pinned drivers & collect trace logs. Target: Fri morning.
3) Add temporary test guard: skip flaky test in CI + create ticket to re-enable after fix (owner: Eli). Short-term to keep rollout moving.
4) Fallback policy: if async flush fails, route to safe-sync path (engineering design exists). Could be toggled via feature flag. Evaluate risk/regression.

Decision points to resolve in the 1:1
- Do we prioritize deterministic harness (long-term fix) or apply a temporary skip to progress rollout this sprint? Trade-offs: speed vs. tech debt.
- If we go temp-skip, define timeline for re-enabling and owner.

Concrete actions (what I want to leave with)
- Eli: push minimal repro into repos/integration/harness + attach repro logs to JIRA INF-3245 by 2027-03-10. (owner: Eli, due: 2027-03-10)
- Eli + Noah: schedule 2h infra pairing and share calendar invite (owner: Eli, coord by Priya, due: 2027-03-11)
- Priya: draft a short status note for the team channel explaining temporary test guard and mitigation plan (owner: Priya, due: 2027-03-11)
- Priya/Eli: decide on fallback feature-flag approach and add RFC stub (owner: Eli to draft, Priya to review, due: 2027-03-17)

Career/feedback prompts (to use only if time)
- "What's one project you want to own next quarter that scares you a little? How can I help you make progress?"
- Strength spotlight: note recent initiative on the prototype — highlight ownership and debugging persistence.
- Growth area: encourage clearer stakeholder updates (weekly brief in #team-kv) — small habit: 3-line summary twice weekly.

Risks / unknowns to surface
- If pinned-driver tests pass locally but fail in canary, need to consider infra image drift across regions. That could require infra ops time beyond what we budgeted.
- Potential perf regression from fallback path — add perf microbenchmarks to validate.

Notes to self (phrasing, tone)
- Keep it supportive. Use specific praise around debug persistence. Say: "I noticed how you narrowed the window on the repro — that made triage faster."
- If Eli wants to go deep into technical details, offer to move a deeper follow-up post-1:1. Timebox this conversation.

Follow-ups after the meeting (templated message)
- Short slack: "Thanks for the sync — created actions: INF-3245 repro (Eli), pairing session (Eli+Noah), temp CI guard (Eli), team note (Priya). I'll follow up on Fri AM with status."
- Update JIRA: add acceptance criteria for re-enable and link to repro.

Open questions to ask in the meeting
- "If infra can't allocate pairing time this week, which of the unblock ideas can you own alone for a short-term workaround?"
- "What would success look like by the end of next week?"

Quick timeline view
- Thu 2027-03-10: repro + logs attached.
- Fri 2027-03-11: infra pairing & team note published.
- Wed 2027-03-17: RFC stub + decision on fallback.

Misc links I want handy in the call
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/481
- JIRA: INF-3245 (KV async flush repro)
- Confluence: confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/KV+Cache+Rollout+Notes

End of notes — keep this updated after the sync.
